_note: Phase 1b — qa-compass routing eval (#47's acceptance test). Different shape from the fixture-outcome cases: each case is a SITUATION → expected ROUTE. qa-compass is a model-invoked router (skills/qa-compass/SKILL.md) that maps a QA situation to exactly one skill via its routing signals, or — when nothing fits cleanly — says so plainly and asks one clarifying question rather than forcing a match (SKILL step 6). No fixture/expected-findings.md exists; the rubric is the router's own signals table + steps. POSITIVE cases assert the `**Use:** /skill` token + a rationale that ties the skill's single question to the situation; a mis-route fails the token. NEGATIVE cases (out-of-scope situations) have NO token — route-none correctness rests on must_surface (states nothing fits + asks one clarifying question) and must_not (emits no `**Use:** /` route). The 5 negatives are deliberately outside the test-credibility domain so route-none is unambiguous. As of ADR-0025 / PR #94 the router is the WHOLE-map front door: the three app-driven skills (e2e-impact, audit-orchestrator, contract-guard) ARE wired in and now carry positive-route cases; `route-flake-heal-caveat` guards the whole-map PROVENANCE DISCIPLINE — a green-pushing self-healer must be surfaced with its heal-to-green hazard caveat, never as confident advice (the 'Unexamined/hazard = lead, not advice' rule). As of ADR-0027 the router has a SEQUENCE mode: a lifecycle/workflow ask ('walk me through QA before merge') returns an ORDERED stage path, entry-anchored to where the change sits, not a single point-route; `seq-before-code` and `seq-pre-merge` guard it (the latter asserts entry-anchoring via must_not — a pre-merge path must NOT start at /test-plan). `anchors` exist only for the offline heuristic judge; the LLM judge grades `claim` directly.

cases.invoke: /qa-compass I'm about to build a checkout feature and want to know what to test before I write any code

must_surface.claim: Routes to `/test-plan` and explains why: the situation is deciding what to test before any code exists — test-plan's single question.

cases.invoke: /qa-compass the AI just generated a big test file for my API service — are the tests actually complete or missing cases?

must_surface.claim: Routes to `/coverage-review` and explains why: AI-written tests already exist and the question is which cases are missing / where assertions are loose.

cases.invoke: /qa-compass this test passes but I don't trust it — would it still pass if the code it covers broke? prove it

must_surface.claim: Routes to `/audit-test` and explains why: a passing test is distrusted and the ask is to prove it catches a regression — by mutation, not reasoning.

cases.invoke: /qa-compass my Playwright spec is red with a locator timeout — diagnose and fix it

must_surface.claim: Routes to `/debug-test` and explains why: a Playwright spec is actively red (locator/timing) and needs diagnosis and routing of the fix.

cases.invoke: /qa-compass I'm about to merge this branch — am I safe to ship?

must_surface.claim: Routes to `/qa-pass` and explains why: the situation is the branch-level am-I-safe-to-merge / ship decision — the single question /qa-pass answers.

must_not.claim: Must NOT tell the user to run the atomic shippability skills (coverage-review, audit-test, qa-review) by hand — /qa-pass calls them for you (SKILL step 4).

cases.invoke: /qa-compass I changed the checkout API and some shared components — which of my Playwright E2E specs actually exercise this diff?

must_surface.claim: Routes to `/e2e-impact` and explains why: there is a diff and the question is which Playwright/Cypress E2E specs it plausibly hits — e2e-impact's single question.

cases.invoke: /qa-compass I've got a suspicious passing test and I'm not sure whether Stryker, Tautest, or something else is the right prover for my stack — pick the tool for me

must_surface.claim: Routes to `/audit-orchestrator` and explains why: the ask is to pick the right prover for the stack (unit -> Stryker/Tautest, app-driven -> audit-test) — its stack-aware routing, distinct from reaching for /audit-test directly.

cases.invoke: /qa-compass my frontend E2E suite went red and I think the backend team changed a field in the API response — does it still match the contract?

must_surface.claim: Routes to `/contract-guard` and explains why: a frontend E2E went red on a suspected backend response/contract change, and the question is whether the response still matches the published contract — contract-guard's single question.

cases.invoke: /qa-compass my Playwright tests are flaky — should I just use a self-healing tool to auto-fix them?

must_surface.claim: Routes to `/debug-test` flake mode (detect -> quarantine -> route the cause) rather than a self-healer.
Surfaces self-healers only with their heal-to-green / masks-a-regression caveat — a credibility hazard, not advice (the provenance discipline for a green-pushing tool).

cases.invoke: /qa-compass I'm starting a new checkout feature and want to do QA properly from planning through to shipping — walk me through the whole path

must_surface.claim: Emits an ordered stage PATH (sequence mode), not a single point-route, and anchors the entry at Plan because no code exists yet.
States the path is a la carte — run as few or as many as you need; each stage stands alone (a recommendation, not a mandate).

any: run as few or as many

cases.invoke: /qa-compass I've finished a feature and its tests — walk me through the QA steps to run, in order, before I merge

must_surface.claim: Emits an ordered path and anchors the entry at Coverage/Audit because tests already exist — the sequence is tailored to where the change sits.
States the path is a la carte — run as few or as many as you need; each stage stands alone.

any: run as few or as many

must_not.claim: Does not anchor the path at Plan — planning is past (code and tests exist), so it emits no /test-plan step (entry-anchoring, not an untailored seven-stage dump).
